ai.description: This toad reaches 4–6 cm. It is olive-brown with dark dorsal spots and a pale belly. Distinctive features include a smooth skin texture and a lack of visible tympanum.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Scutiger occidentalis* is distinguished by the presence of prominent, black-tipped nuptial spines on the inner fingers of males, which are absent in other Indian *Scutiger*.
ai.habitat: *Scutiger occidentalis* inhabits high-altitude streams and rocky meadows in the Himalayas, typically found at elevations between 3,000 and 4,500 meters.
ai.behavior: The Ladakh Pelobatid Toad is primarily nocturnal, emerging at night to forage for insects along the banks of high-altitude streams and rocky mountain slopes.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Scutiger occidentalis* breeds in high-altitude streams during summer (June–July). Females lay small clutches of large, unpigmented eggs attached to submerged stones.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Scutiger occidentalis* is endemic to the high-altitude regions of Ladakh, India, typically inhabiting cold, alpine streams at elevations between 3,500 and 5,000 meters.
ai.callDescription: The Ladakh Pelobatid Toad emits a low-pitched, rhythmic croak, often heard as a series of short, pulsed notes near cold, high-altitude mountain streams and seepages.
